issue_context.title: HTTP/2 support
issue_context.body:
First of all, congratulations, this library looks fantastic.

I've looked through the documentation and can't find any mention of HTTP/2 support. Is there anything in the works? Would it be easy or difficult to implement?

Thanks!
comments:
Hi, thank you for the interest!
At the moment HTTP/2 is not supported, but we are working on it ;)

@delvedor Thanks! I'll also ask this here - I believe the library could be sped up by eliminating a function call. Fastify responds using something like `reply.send({ hello: 'world' })`. Koa responds simply by `ctx.body = 'world'`. Thoughts on this?
I think we should implement HTTP/2 support using the `--expose-http2` flag in Node 8.
Yes, please! Having http2 would make me try this instead of express for my next API :-)

If someone will use Fastify and Server Push — it really works. Pitfall is that `:path` must starts with `/` otherwise `stream` event will be not fired on client (and it is not Fastify issue, the same if use http2 module directly).

review_comments: If a flag is required then it's not "available" in terms of being a feature of a downstream product.

This option naming feels weird.

How about:
```js
http2: Boolean,
http1: Boolean
```
or:
```js
https: {
  allowHTTP1: Boolean,
  allowHTTP2: Boolean
},
http: {
  allowHTTP1: Boolean,
  allowHTTP2: Boolean
  // Caveat: Not yet possible to enable both simultaneously
}
```

I don't like this either. The benefit of the current API is that it's transparent, as instead of going to `http`  and `https`  it just goes to `http2`. `allowHTTP1` option is from the `http2`  module in core.
That is not correct. Because `resolve` assumes the file is run from the root of the project.
